column1: # MANUALLY MANAGED - INITIALLY GENERATED by `homm3 mac migrate` from the
# reviewed config/mac inventories and hand-owned after admission.
# Library, runtime and compiler-support code: label only; the extent
# is the functions.tsv row at the same offset. Not game functions.
# owner: msl_c, msl_cxx, cw_runtime, compiler_generated, or empty when unknown (see homm3.mac.tables).
# Offsets are relative to PEF code section 0; lowercase 0x hex.

column5: evidence

HERO getMoraleDescription at 0xf88fc and getLuckDescription at 0xf8efc both call code 0:0x948 after adding 0x1c to TTextResource, passing text index 438 in r4. The complete 16-byte body loads vector data at receiver+8, scales the index by four, adds it to the data pointer and returns the element address; BLR is at 0x954 and the next prologue starts 0x958. The pinned MSL vector<T>::operator[](size_type) forwards through its POD indexer, and CodeWarrior emits the named `.__vc__Q23std10vector<Pc>CFUl` call in the shared HERO candidate. Runtime template identity only, with no Windows VA claim.

The 125 direct callers include TAdventureMapWindow construction of its vector<widget*>. The callee compares size with capacity, doubles capacity through reviewed POD-vector reserve 0x47b0 when full, copies one four-byte pointer from r4 to data[size], increments size, and returns at 0x2158; the next function starts at 0x215c. The neutral label covers the pointer-vector operation without claiming one template spelling for all callers.

The canonical MSL pointer-vector push_back used in AI_PLAYER valueOfHiring emits three calls to this compressed-pair second() accessor. The pinned callee at 0:0x215c consists solely of blr: the receiver is already in r3, so it returns the member reference unchanged. Its next function starts with mflr at 0x2160. Library template identity only.

Canonical TTextResource::operator[] calls getText, indexing its m_text vector at object+0x1c. The KB Mac view now emits named std::vector<char*>::operator[](int) from that shared inline body. Retail KB setter repeatedly adds +0x1c to the resource before calling 0x2a0c; its four instructions load vector first pointer at +8, scale index by 4, return element address, and end with BLR 0x2a18 before the next entry 0x2a1c. Runtime template identity only, not a vector-body score; the byte-identical 0x948 entry is not used by this caller.

NewfullMap::newfullMapFn005042C0 calls the retained MSL string compare at code 0x127218. The candidate's named call takes string receiver, position, count, byte pointer and length in r3-r7; the retail body bounds-checks the position, calls the bounded byte comparison at 0x28b11c and returns at 0x4314. The next prologue at 0x4318 bounds the full helper. Runtime call identity only.

KB setter's char-pointer assignment compiles through a source-view inline operator=(const char*) into named std::string::assign(const char*, unsigned long): strlen first, then receiver/pointer/length in r3/r4/r5. Retail repeats the same call sequence at 0x116848..0x11685c and calls this callee at 0x445c. The callee passes length to string storage helper 0x4ad4, copies with .memcpy, returns receiver; own prologue follows preceding BLR, final BLR 0x44bc, next destructor prologue 0x44c0 bound all 100 bytes. Runtime identity and ABI evidence only; no candidate library-body score.

KB destroys each stack formatString temporary after assignment, passing receiver r3 and deleting flag -1 r4 to this string destructor at 0x44c0. Callee updates shared-storage count, frees storage only at zero and conditionally frees receiver for positive flag. Own prologue follows assign BLR 0x44bc, final BLR 0x4564 and next constructor prologue 0x4568 bound all 168 bytes. Library identity only, not a template-body score.

The named CodeWarrior MSL basic_string(const char*, const allocator&) constructor is emitted at type_artifact::getDescription candidate +0x50; the source-view declaration follows the pinned MSL string header. Retail getDescription calls 0x4568 at code 0xf759c with destination r3, artifact description r4 and stack allocator r5. The callee stores an empty handle, calls strlen on r4, checks the length and initializes from the source range. Its prologue follows the prior destructor BLR at 0x4564, final BLR is 0x4640 and the next prologue starts 0x4644. Full 220-byte pinned PEF span was SHA-verified. Runtime library identity only.

The KB showCongrats Mac view emits the named std::string default constructor with its local string receiver at candidate +0x24; retail calls 0x46c8 with its stack string receiver at 0x115c5c. Callee allocates a 16-byte representation, seeds storage/count and zero length, writes the empty terminator, then returns its receiver. Own prologue 0x46c8, final BLR 0x47ac and next constructor prologue 0x47b0 bound all 232 bytes. Runtime library identity only, not a candidate string-body score.

AI_PLAYER valueOfHiring's canonical MSL vector<pathCell*> push_back emits this named POD reserve call at candidate +0x464; Mac retail calls the body at 0:0x47b0 from 0:0x354b4. The callee compares requested capacity, allocates and copies pointer entries, frees the previous buffer, and updates capacity. Its final return precedes the next body at 0x48bc. Library template identity only.

Ten calls in the puzzle-window global initializer construct one-word masks from value 1 before shifting each by offsets 0..9. This complete three-instruction body masks r4 to ten bits, stores the word at receiver+0 and returns at 0x4f58 before the shift operator at 0x4f5c. The installed MSL bitset(unsigned long) definition performs this mask for N<32, and a CodeWarrior game source view emits the exact bitset<10> constructor symbol. Runtime template identity only.

The puzzle-window initializer calls this body after constructing each bitset<10>(1), passing shifts 0..9. It shifts the receiver's word left by r4, clears higher words if any, masks the low word to ten bits and returns at BLR 0x5050 before the next prologue at 0x5054. The neutral label records the MSL bitset<10> shift operation without guessing the emitted operator mangling.

Recruit update calls the retained MSL vector<char*>::begin accessor at code 0x14f4dc. The complete body at 0x5eec returns receiver+8 then blr; its next neighbor begins at 0x5ef4. The emitted MWOB call is named .begin__Q23std10vector<Pc>CFv, and the Mac image has 349 direct calls to this small accessor. Runtime call identity only.

The selected Seer Hut view emits this exact CodeWarrior MSL compressed_pair_imp constructor for vector<type_dialog_resource> at caller +0x44. The retail shared four-skill dialog helper calls 0x66a4 at 0x164e6c with its stack vector address in r3 and zero capacity in r4, then zeros size/data. The entire target body is `stw r4,0(r3); blr`, bounded by its return at 0x66a8 and the next prologue at 0x66ac; all eight bytes are pinned by SHA. Loader xrefs identify 16 code callers, including the Seer Hut helper and TOWN dialog setup. This binds one emitted library-template identity, not a game helper or broader alias.

AI markMultiheadedEnemy destroys its local vector<long> at 0:0x21f1c..0x21f24 with deleting flag zero. This named CodeWarrior template destructor frees backing data at receiver+8 and conditionally deletes the receiver. Entry follows preceding BLR at 0x7458 and final BLR at 0x74b4 precedes the vector constructor. Runtime template identity only.

AI markMultiheadedEnemy constructs its stack vector<long> at caller 0:0x21d18..0x21d20, passing vector address in r3 and zero in r4. This named CodeWarrior template constructor stores r4 at receiver+0 and returns. Preceding BLR at 0x74b4 and next prologue at 0x74c0 bound the complete eight-byte body. Runtime template identity only.

The full body is addi r3,r3,8; blr, ending before the next function at 0x8108. Mac has 100 direct calls, including combatWindow::showMessages on its vector<string*> and AI_PLAYER vector scans; callers then load the vector data pointer from the returned slot. This is a separately retained MSL vector storage accessor with the same bytes as 0x5eec. The neutral label does not assert a particular template instantiation or emitted symbol.

Retail KB formatString temporary assignment passes destination r3, source r4, position zero r5 and npos r6 to 0x1c094 at 0x116914..0x116924. Source-view inline std::string::operator=(const string&) now exposes the same named assign(const string&, unsigned long, unsigned long) ABI. Callee uses source string length and storage, returns destination; final BLR 0x1c2e0 and next prologue 0x1c2e4 bound all 592 bytes. Library call identity only, not a template-body score.

The pinned CodeWarrior MSL string header defines operator+=(char) as append(1, char); HERO type_artifact::getDescription emits the exact named append(unsigned long,char) call at candidate +0x94. Retail calls 0x1c388 at code 0xf75d8 with count one in r4 and character in r5. The callee checks count and capacity, grows string storage, then writes the byte through memset. Its final BLR at 0x1c47c and next append(const char*,unsigned long) prologue at 0x1c480 bound the full 248-byte SHA-verified body. Runtime library identity only.

KB secondary-skill text uses canonical string += char-pointer statements. Retail first calls strlen at 0x116db0 then passes receiver/pointer/length in r3/r4/r5 to 0x1c480 at 0x116dc0, repeating at 0x116dec..0x116dfc. Source-view inline operator+= exposes the same named append(const char*, unsigned long) call. Callee grows storage via 0x4ad4, then .memcpy at 0x28aa6c, returns receiver; final BLR 0x1c4fc and next prologue 0x1c500 bound all 128 bytes. Runtime identity only, not a library-body score.

The TOWN creature reward helper passes destination string r3, temporary source r4, position zero r5 and npos r6 at 0x1b5a2c..0x1b5a3c, matching the canonical operator+=(const string&) source-view expansion. This callee copies source length/data, grows destination via 0x4ad4 and copies through .memcpy; preceding char-append BLR at 0x1c4fc, final BLR at 0x1c624 and next prologue at 0x1c628 bound all 296 bytes. Runtime identity only.

normalDialog copies TNormalDialogInfo by value after calculateNormalDialogSize; its emitted std::string copy constructor call takes destination and source handles in r3/r4. Retail calls code0:0x1c628 at +0x134, and that callee copies the representation pointer, increments shared count when nonzero, or constructs a new 16-byte representation when needed. Final BLR at 0x1c6ec and next prologue at 0x1c6f0 bound all 200 bytes. Library identity only.

The installed CodeWarrior MSL vector classifies this custom record as non-POD (default class_has_trivial_* traits are false), and its __vector_imp<T,false>::push_back definition matches the selected view's emitted symbol at caller +0x88. Retail's shared four-skill dialog helper calls 0x1c6f0 at 0x164eb4 with vector receiver r3 and an eight-byte record r4. The full 0xa0-byte callee tests size against capacity, reserves when full, conditionally copies both words into data[size] with constructed-local cleanup metadata, and increments size. Its preceding helper returns at 0x1c6ec, this one at 0x1c78c, and clear begins at 0x1c790; 23 linked callers include Seer Hut and TOWN dialog builders. This binds only the non-POD library-template identity.

TOWN reward helper calls vector<type_dialog_resource>::clear at 0x1b5b6c after its optional extendedDialog. The callee computes 8-byte element distance from size and data pointer, then stores zero to vector size at +4; prior push-back BLR at 0x1c78c, own BLR at 0x1c7c4 and next vector destructor prologue at 0x1c7c8 bound 56 bytes. Runtime template identity only.

The selected non-POD MSL view emits this vector destructor at doProgressDialog candidate +0xc4. Retail's shared four-skill dialog helper calls 0x1c7c8 at 0x164ee4 with the constructed vector receiver and deleting flag -1. Its full body calls the reviewed vector::clear at 0x1c790, frees the data pointer if present, then conditionally frees the vector receiver for a positive deleting flag, as in the installed MSL vector lifetime. The preceding clear returns at 0x1c7c4 and this body returns at 0x1c828; 18 code callers include the Seer Hut helper and other dialog builders. This is a library-template identity, not a game helper.

MSL bitset<48>::test takes receiver and bit index, bounds-checks against 48, and returns the selected bit. Repeated calls from mapcell, game, advmgr and viewwrld are library operations, not game helper boundaries. Final BLR at 0x1c90c precedes the next body.

The installed MSL string header implements replace(pos, removed_length, inserted_count, char) with position and length checks, copy-on-write storage, tail move, character fill and terminator update. Retail calls this body with string receiver r3, position r4, removed length r5, inserted count r6 and character r7. The seven sites include erase() with r4=0/r5=npos/r6=r7=0, erase(pos) in ResourceManager, and one comma insertion with r6=1/r7=','. The body checks string size at +0, allocates a new 16-byte representation if needed, calls the fill operation at 0x28b040, and returns at 0x1cc5c; the next prologue starts at 0x1cc60. This neutral label records an MSL string operation, not a game helper.

advManager::townGate calls this with the game player vector and an index. It multiplies the index by the verified Mac playerData stride 0x15c, adds the vector data pointer at +8, and returns. BLR 0x1e794; next body starts 0x1e798. MSL vector element access, not an authored game helper.

AI calculateReserve destroys its local vector<type_creature_value> through this named CodeWarrior destructor. It calls the verified clear at 0x25ca4, frees backing data through 0x268b2c and conditionally deletes the object for a positive deleting flag. Final blr at 0x25a60 and next body starts at 0x25a64. Runtime template identity only.

AI calculateReserve calls this named std::vector<type_creature_value>::clear at its reserve body +0x9c; the vector destructor independently calls it at 0:0x25a24. It reads 12-byte element count and data at vector+4/+8, runs the element destruction loop and stores zero size at +4. Final blr at 0x25cdc and next prologue at 0x25ce0 bound the 60-byte body. Runtime template identity only.

The Mac type_AI_combat_data constructor calls this vector<type_monster_data> allocator-capacity constructor with receiver in r3 and zero in r4, then zeros vector size and data at +4/+8. A CodeWarrior -O3 probe emits the exact named compressed_pair_imp hunk and the same eight bytes, stw r4,0(r3); blr. The preceding vector destructor ends at 0x26620 and initializeCreatures begins at 0x2662c. MSL template identity only.

Returns receiver+8. Four chooseMelee call sites use it while walking type_AI_combat_data::m_creatures, already authored as std::vector indexing. BLR at 0x28ae0 bounds the body. MSL vector storage accessor, not a game helper.

Fourteen calls in five ai_combat/ai_player functions destroy stack type_AI_combat_data objects, whose first member is m_creatures. The generated type_AI_combat_data destructor at 0x28a7c calls this body on that first member; this callee is the MSL vector<type_monster_data> deleting-flag destructor, not an authored game helper. It clears through 0x2a9e8, frees vector data at +8 if present, optionally deletes the vector receiver for a positive flag, and returns at 0x29c04; the next body starts at 0x29c08. All observed stack callers pass flag zero.

The reviewed 0x29ba4 vector destructor calls this clear body. It computes data + size * 0x40, walks the 64-byte Mac type_monster_data elements, then zeros vector size at +4. BLR at 0x2aa1c and the next entry begins at 0x2aa20. Generated MSL container cleanup only.

AI calculateReserve constructs its vector<type_creature_value> storage with this named Metrowerks compressed_pair_imp constructor. The retail call reaches 0:0x2bb9c with vector address in r3 and zero in r4; the entire callee stores r4 at +0 and returns. Candidate CodeWarrior emits the same 8-byte named hunk; next function begins at 0x2bba4. Runtime template identity only.

AI_PLAYER valueOfHiring constructs its vector<HeroDestination> capacity pair at caller 0:0x35270. The emitted named CodeWarrior hunk receives the pair in r3 and zero in r4. The pinned Mac callee at 0:0x33a70 is exactly stw r4,0(r3); blr, ending at 0x33a78 before the next function. Library template identity only.

AI calculateReserve sorts its vector's 12-byte value records through this named std::sort instantiation. The callee computes record count from a 12-byte pointer difference, uses insertion sort for runs of 20 or fewer and dispatches larger ranges through the library sorter. Final blr at 0x3a1e0 and next prologue at 0x3a1e4 bound the 552-byte body. Runtime template call identity only.

Computes the distance from a four-byte element pointer to a three-word vector's end, shifts following words down, decrements the size word at +4, and returns the erased iterator. army::eraseItem and TRmgVoronoi::removeEdge call it for their authored vector.erase operations; other callers use the same four-byte vector operation. BLR at 3a884; next independent insertion entry at 3a888. MSL vector instantiation, not a game helper.

Three-word vector insertion checks capacity, grows storage when needed, and copies/fills four-byte elements. type_AI_player::canTradeResources calls it twice for the authored baseCost.insert(begin,count,0) and unitCost.insert(begin,count,0); RMG uses the same template family. BLR at 3ac18, followed by a distinct prologue at 3ac1c. MSL vector instantiation, not a game helper.

AI calculateReserve appends a source-owned 12-byte type_creature_value record through this named vector instantiation at 0:0x3ad64. The callee grows vector storage through 0x3c370 when full, copies three words into the next slot and increments size. Final blr at 0x3ae08 and next prologue at 0x3ae0c bound the 168-byte body. Runtime template call identity only.

Library template instantiated by source-owned type_AI_creature_purchaser::m_creatures (include/ai_player.h). Three buyCreatures calls pass purchaser+0x2c (stack+0xa4), matching this vector member and the emitted CodeWarrior destructor symbol. Full body null-checks this, calls clear at 0x3b06c, frees data at this+8 through 0x268b2c, and deletes this iff the signed-short deleting flag is positive; returns this. Final blr at 0x3b108 and next entry at 0x3b10c bound the span. This is a retained runtime binding, not a candidate template-body match.

A vector<pathCell> clear routine: this+4 is the size, this+8 is data, and the loop stride is 0x1e, the verified pathCell size. It resets size to zero and returns at 0x3b144; next function begins 0x3b148. Runtime template identity only.

Eleven ai_player/findpath callers reach this scalar-deleting vector<pathCell> destructor. It calls the 0x3b10c clear routine, frees this+8, conditionally frees this when the signed-short deleting flag is positive, and returns this. Final BLR 0x3b1a8; next prologue 0x3b1ac. Runtime template identity only.

AI_PLAYER valueOfHiring calls this named vector<HeroDestination> destructor at 0:0x357ac with deleting flag zero. The 100-byte body calls its element deleter at 0x3c70c, frees backing data and conditionally deletes the vector itself; its final return precedes the next prologue at 0x3b210. Runtime template identity only.

The MSL bitset<9>::test body bounds-checks the index against nine and extracts the bit. AI-player and army-group callers use the authored grouped-alignment bitset and its test operation. Final BLR at 0x3b2f0 precedes bitset<144>::test at 0x3b2f4. Library template identity only.

HERO removeArtifact emits named std::bitset<144>::test(unsigned long) at object +0x88; its Mac caller passes indices 0..143 and reaches 0x3b2f4. Callee bounds-checks 144, selects one of five 32-bit words, masks the indexed bit and returns bool. Final BLR 0x3b3d4 and next function prologue 0x3b3d8 bound all 228 bytes. Runtime identity only, not a candidate template-body match.

Twenty-four Mac AI tactical call sites construct four copies at a time. The body zeros the receiver's three vector words, takes the source vector's size and backing pointer from r4, then delegates the element copy to 0x46f54. BLR at 0x46a04; the next body starts at 0x46a08. Library vector copy construction, not an authored combat helper.

makeArtifactComponentMask constructs its source std::bitset<144> through this body; campaign scenario and map loading callers also construct five-word bitsets. It zeros receiver words +0,+4,+8,+12,+16 and returns at 0x5afe4 before the next entry. MSL template construction, not an authored game helper.
Full-TU artifact CodeWarrior hunk .__eq__Q23std10bitset<19>CFRCQ23std10bitset<19> (0x20 bytes) matches these bytes outside relocated words and fills the proven span (homm3 mac inventory object lead).

Artifact, hero and swap-manager callers pass a four-byte artifact-slot mask and slot index to this MSL bitset<19>::test body. It checks index against 19, uses the installed MSL bitset::test bounds-error path, extracts the requested bit and returns bool; BLR at 0x5b0f4 precedes bitset<19>::set. The authored Windows source already uses the bitset and its indexing/test operations. Library template identity only.

Artifact mask construction and initializeArtifactTraits call this MSL bitset<19>::set body. It bounds-checks index against 19, then sets or clears the selected word bit according to r5 and returns its receiver. The installed CodeWarrior bitset header has the same operation; BLR at 0x5b1dc precedes bitset<144>::set. Both authored Windows callers already use set. Library template identity only.

Artifact, campaign, game, hero and RMG callers pass a five-word artifact-component mask, index and bool to this MSL bitset<144>::set body. It checks the index against 144, selects word index/bit, then sets or clears the bit and returns the receiver. The installed CodeWarrior bitset header confirms this operation; BLR at 0x5b2c4 precedes artifact initialization at 0x5b2c8. Existing Windows callers express bitset access in source. Library template identity only.
Two calls during CMapHeaderData copy construction return the data field of a 12-byte vector record at this+8; BLR 0x64270. The specific instantiation is not established.
Two CMapHeaderData copy sites pass a vector and index; the body returns data at +8 plus index times four, BLR 0x670c8. Runtime vector element access only.

This retained deleting wrapper tests the vector receiver, calls the shared vector destructor at 0x68da4 with a zero flag, and calls scalar delete at 0x268b2c only when its own deleting flag is positive. The BLR at 0x672cc precedes an independent zero-initializing vector constructor at 0x672d0. It has 43 direct calls in unfinished campaign and game bodies. Several POD-vector instantiations can fold to this code, so the neutral label intentionally makes no element-type or Windows-VA claim.

The pinned SavedGameHeader and campaign-brief constructors call this on CMapHeaderData::m_placeholders at+0x20. A CodeWarrior -O3 probe with the same MSL vector<int> emits the named 20-byte __vector_pod<unsigned long> default constructor, exactly the five target instructions zeroing capacity, size and data. Library template identity only.

The same constructors call this on NewSMapHeader::m_availableHeroes at+0x2b4. A CodeWarrior -O3 probe using the pinned MSL bitset<156> emits this exact 28-byte constructor: zero five words and return. Library template identity only.

Five constructor/copy sites in campaignbrief, campaignwindow, game and singleselectionwindow pass a vector record plus begin/end pointers. The body computes a four-byte element count, copies or grows the vector and updates size; BLR 0x68494. Runtime range assignment, without a unique element type claim.

Campaignbrief copy construction calls this range assignment at 0x64234. It counts eight-byte elements, copies a scalar word and assigns a std::string at +4 through MSL 0x1c094, with string destruction on shrink; BLR 0x68684. Runtime container operation only.

Campaignbrief generated destructors call this tree-node cleanup at 0x67324 and 0x670fc. It recursively destroys both child links, destroys a string member at +0x14 and deletes the node; BLR 0x68704. Runtime tree cleanup only.

Campaignbrief CMapHeaderData copy construction calls this tree assignment at 0x64250. It clears the destination tree, copies the source root and count, then repairs the sentinel/leftmost link; BLR 0x687d0. Runtime tree operation only.

CMapHeaderData constructors call this on m_heroPlayerSetups at+0x29c with the comparator byte by reference. CodeWarrior -O3 with the pinned MSL map<int,type_map_hero_info> emits the same 40-byte __tree constructor shape and full mangled symbol; it initializes the tree sentinel, zero count and comparator. The target's TOC load is link-specific. Library template identity only.

Campaignbrief appends a CMapHeaderData value at 0x658b0 and 0x65b04. The body grows a vector if full, copy-constructs a 0x498-byte element, advances size and returns; BLR 0x68910. Runtime vector append, not a new game helper.

Seven calls from compiler-generated destruction in CMapHeaderData, CampaignScenarioPreview, SCampaign, ScenarioStruct, SavedGameHeader and game. The body calls 0x68f40 to clear four-byte trivial elements and zero the vector size, frees data at +8, and optionally deletes the vector receiver when the delete flag is positive. BLR at 0x68e04 precedes another vector destructor. The common body does not identify a unique template instantiation.

Campaignbrief generated destruction calls this vector destructor at 0x678f4. It clears through 0x69504, frees data at +8 and optionally deletes the receiver when the flag is positive; BLR 0x68ecc. The element instantiation is not established.
Game container cleanup calls this body at 0xdaa34. It walks eight-byte elements backward, destroys the std::string member at +4 and sets vector size to zero; BLR 0x68f3c. Runtime vector clear only.

The 0x68da4 deleting destructor calls this body; customcampaign and game also call it directly at 0x99aa4 and 0xdb33c. It advances over four-byte trivial elements and zeros vector size; BLR 0x68f74. Runtime vector clear only.
Game clears a tree at 0xdb3b4 and 0xdc590. This body destroys nodes through 0x68688, zeroes the root and count, and resets its sentinel link; BLR 0x68fc4. Runtime tree clear only.

The same four SCampaign copy sites pass the +0x48 vector and begin/end pointers. This body counts 20-byte MapScore elements, assigns or grows the vector and ends at BLR 0x6b7f8 before the next function. Generated vector range assignment, not an authored helper.

Five customcampaign calls destroy local vector<hero> objects. The callee checks the receiver, clears elements through 0x6c748, deletes vector data at +8, and optionally deletes the receiver when the CodeWarrior delete flag is positive. BLR at 0x6c744 precedes the clear body. This neutral label identifies the vector operation, not a proven mangled instantiation.

The installed CodeWarrior MSL vector<bool>::num_words(size_type) computes (capacity - 1) / 32 + 1. This complete four-instruction body subtracts one, shifts right by five, adds one and returns at 0x72250; the next body begins at 0x72254. Called during TPickANumber cleanup in cmbtmgr and spells. Runtime template operation only, without a Windows helper claim.

Eagle Eye call sites construct one-word iterator temporaries from a set position. The complete body copies r4 to the receiver and returns at 0x768e4; adjacent 0x768e8 returns an object's field at +0xc. This is a container iterator constructor, not a combat game helper.

The body grows three-word vector storage when full and appends one 0x18-byte element. combatManager::placeObstacle, setupAndLoadObstacles and castSpell call it where the authored code pushes combat obstacles into m_obstacles. Final BLR at 0x77038 precedes a distinct prologue at 0x7703c. MSL vector insertion, not a game helper.

Seven direct calls from TCombatWindow::combatMessage, TSpellbookWindow::getSpellDescription and textEntryWidget::draw/setupDisplayString correspond to authored std::string::substr calls.
